title: Fighting AI Slop in Science Papers
key_facts: arXiv announced a limit of two submissions per month per submitter, after receiving 40,363 submissions in September 2026 (20,569 in September 2024, 9,869 in September 2016).
The month also produced almost 9,000 support tickets; moderators see more thin, 'salami' and dense AI-written papers.
In May arXiv imposed a one-year ban for unchecked AI content.
Seoul National University and the University of Minnesota published 'Science or Slop?' with SciSlopBench, built from 390 AI-generated papers each paired with a human-written one.
The benchmark identified the AI paper in 85.9% of pairs; SciSlopHarness cut the remaining AI-human gap by 63% against the strongest revision baseline.
The new paper scored 'moderate' (40/100) on its own demo.
quote_evidence: Last week, preprint server arXiv announced that it will be instituting a new rate-limiting policy for submitters, who will now be capped at two submissions per month.
The benchmark correctly identified the AI-generated paper in 85.9% of these comparisons.
Our moderators are observing an increase in thin papers of narrow scope, as well as 'salami' papers.
why_it_matters_hint: A flood of low-quality AI-written papers strains the review system scientists rely on.
event_date: arXiv announcement about a week before 4 Oct 2026 (Hacker News discussion on a Thursday, 1 Oct); research paper date not stated
notes: arXiv announcement described as 'last week' in the 4 Oct article, so lowered 5 to 4 as not new today. Benchmark figures are the authors' own.
